notes: Fraud / social-engineering patterns for bank call-center calls. Triggers are case-insensitive phrases matched on word boundaries (apostrophes are ignored, so "don't" == "dont"); a trigger starting with "re:" is a raw regex. If `requires_all` is present, every group must have at least one hit and `triggers` is ignored. `severity` is the risk score (0-1) contributed when the pattern matches. Sources are top-level consumer-protection pages; verify before citing in the pitch.

patterns.name: Account takeover: contact change + money movement
patterns.description: Caller changes the phone number, email or mailing address on file and, in the same call, asks to move money. Classic account-takeover sequence: redirect one-time codes and callbacks to the fraudster, then drain the account.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Do not process the change or the payment in this call. Verify identity by calling back on the phone number already on file (not the new one), and place a hold on outgoing transfers per account-takeover policy.
patterns.say_this: For your security, I'll call you back on the number we already have on file before making any changes or payments.

patterns.name: Contact details change request
patterns.description: Request to change phone, email or address. Usually legitimate, but it is the first step of most account takeovers, so it raises risk slightly and combines with other signals.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Complete step-up verification before changing contact details, and send a confirmation to the old contact method.
patterns.say_this: Before I update your contact details, I'll send a quick confirmation to the phone or email we already have on file.

patterns.name: Urgent wire to a new payee
patterns.description: Caller insists a wire or transfer must go out right now, often to a new recipient. Urgency is the most common lever in authorized-push-payment fraud.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Slow the call down. Ask who the recipient is and how the customer knows them; offer a cooling-off hold before releasing the wire.
patterns.say_this: I want to make sure this payment gets to the right person, so let's take a moment to confirm who the recipient is.

patterns.name: Grandparent / family emergency scam
patterns.description: Customer wants to send money because a grandchild or relative is in jail, in an accident or in the hospital. Scammers impersonate the relative or a lawyer, often with a cloned voice.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Gently pause the transaction. Suggest the customer hang up and call the family member directly on a number they already know before sending anything.
patterns.say_this: Before we send anything, could you call your family member back on a number you already know, just to be sure they're okay?

patterns.name: Gift card payment demand
patterns.description: Someone told the customer to pay with gift cards or read gift-card numbers over the phone. Buying a gift card as a present, or asking about a gift-card charge, is not this pattern.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Explain that gift-card payment demands are always scams. Do not process related withdrawals; offer to report to the FTC.
patterns.say_this: I want to protect you: no real company or agency asks to be paid with gift cards, so let's hold off on this one.

source.name: FTC: Avoiding and reporting gift card scams

patterns.name: Cryptocurrency / crypto ATM payment
patterns.description: Customer is being directed to buy cryptocurrency or deposit cash into a crypto ATM. Common in impersonation, romance and investment scams.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Ask who instructed the crypto purchase. Warn that no bank, agency or business asks customers to move money into crypto to protect it.
patterns.say_this: Can I ask who suggested moving money into crypto? I'd like to make sure no one is pressuring you.

source.name: FTC: What to know about cryptocurrency and scams

patterns.name: Government agency impersonation (IRS / SSA / law enforcement)
patterns.description: Caller references the IRS, Social Security, US Marshals, customs or a warrant to pressure a payment. Agencies do not demand immediate payment by phone.
triggers: social security number has been suspended
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Tell the customer that government agencies never demand payment over the phone. Pause the payment and point them to the agency's official site.
patterns.say_this: Government agencies don't ask for payment over the phone, so let's pause this and check with the agency's official website first.

patterns.name: "Bank fraud department" safe-account scam
patterns.description: Someone claiming to be the bank's fraud department told the customer their account is compromised and to move money to a 'safe' or 'secure' account. Banks never ask this.
triggers: move my money to keep it safe
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Tell the customer clearly: the bank will never ask you to move money to protect it. Do not process the transfer; escalate to the fraud team.
patterns.say_this: I want to reassure you: the bank will never ask you to move your money to keep it safe, so I won't move anything today.

patterns.name: Remote-access software / tech support
patterns.description: Customer installed or was told to install remote-access software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Quick Assist) or let someone 'fix' their computer or bank account.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Advise disconnecting the device from the internet and not logging in to online banking. Lock online access and reset credentials before any transaction.
patterns.say_this: To keep your account safe, please disconnect that device from the internet and don't let anyone access it while we talk.

patterns.name: Secrecy instruction
patterns.description: The customer was told not to tell the bank, family or anyone else about the transaction. Secrecy is a hallmark of social-engineering scams.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Name the red flag kindly: anyone asking you to keep a payment secret from your bank or family is likely a scammer.
patterns.say_this: I understand, and just so you know, anyone who asks you to keep a payment secret from your bank or family is a common warning sign.

patterns.name: Urgency / time pressure
patterns.description: Generic urgency language. Weak on its own (many real calls are urgent) but it compounds other patterns.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Acknowledge the urgency but follow the standard verification steps; urgency is never a reason to skip them.
patterns.say_this: I know this feels urgent, and I'll go as quickly as I can while still keeping your account safe.

patterns.name: Customer being coached by a third party
patterns.description: Customer is relaying instructions from someone else, often still on another line ('he says I need to...', 'they told me not to tell you', 'the man on the other line said'). Long hesitations before simple answers can support this, but the text cue is primary.
triggers: stay on the line with them
they are still on the phone
told me not to tell you
told me not to tell the bank
said not to tell the bank
the man on the other line
the man on the phone said
the woman on the phone said
the lady on the phone said
the guy on the phone said
the agent on the phone said
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Ask calmly whether anyone else is on the line or telling them what to say. Continue only once the customer is alone; offer to call them back on the number on file or bring in a trusted contact.
patterns.say_this: Is anyone else on the line with you right now? It's completely fine, I'd just like to speak with you alone for a moment.

patterns.name: Romance scam
patterns.description: Money going to someone the customer met online and has never met in person, often 'stuck overseas' or needing fees.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Ask how long they have known the recipient and whether they have met in person. Share romance-scam warning signs before processing.
patterns.say_this: May I ask how long you've known this person, and whether you've met in person? I ask everyone sending money abroad.

patterns.name: Overpayment / refund scam
patterns.description: Customer was told they were 'accidentally refunded too much' and must send the difference back.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Check whether any incoming 'refund' actually cleared (often it is a move between the customer's own accounts). Do not send money back.
patterns.say_this: Let's double-check that refund together first, because sometimes it's just money moved between your own accounts.

patterns.name: One-time code redirection
patterns.description: Caller asks to send verification codes to a different device or says they cannot receive codes on the number on file.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Never send one-time codes to an unverified number. Use the number on file or in-branch verification.
patterns.say_this: For your protection, I can only send codes to the number we already have on file.

patterns.name: Investment scam (guaranteed returns)
patterns.description: Promises of guaranteed or unusually high returns, a 'trading platform' or an advisor met online.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Ask how they found the opportunity and whether they have withdrawn any profits. Recommend checking the firm with regulators before sending funds.
patterns.say_this: Have you been able to withdraw any of your profits yet? I'd suggest checking the firm with regulators before sending more.

patterns.name: Prize / lottery / sweepstakes fee
patterns.description: Customer must pay a fee or taxes to claim a prize or lottery winnings.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Explain that real prizes never require paying a fee first. Pause the payment.
patterns.say_this: Real prizes never ask you to pay a fee first, so I'd recommend we don't send this payment.

patterns.name: Changed payment instructions (BEC / vendor fraud)
patterns.description: Caller says a vendor, contractor, title company or landlord sent 'new' wire instructions. Typical business-email-compromise and real-estate closing fraud.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Recommend confirming the new instructions by calling the vendor on a known number (not one from the email) before sending.
patterns.say_this: Before we send this, please call the vendor on a number you already know to confirm their new bank details.

patterns.name: Cash withdrawal for courier pickup
patterns.description: Customer is withdrawing a large amount of cash that someone will pick up in person or that must be mailed. Growing pattern in grandparent and government-impersonation scams.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Ask who is collecting the cash. Legitimate agencies and relatives' lawyers do not send couriers; escalate before releasing large cash withdrawals.
patterns.say_this: Can I ask who is collecting the cash? Banks and government agencies never send someone to pick up money.

patterns.name: Request for full credentials
patterns.description: Someone asks for, or the customer reports being asked for, full secrets: social security number, online banking login or password, full card number, PIN, or account number to 'process a refund' or 'claim a prize'. Banks and legitimate companies don't collect these on an unsolicited call.
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Remind the customer that the bank and legitimate companies never ask for full card numbers, PINs or passwords on a call. If any were shared, lock online access, reissue the card and reset credentials.
patterns.say_this: Just so you know, we'll never ask for your full card number, PIN or passwords, and nobody else should either.

source.name: FTC: How to recognize and avoid phishing scams

patterns.name: Verification evasion
patterns.description: Caller dodges identity or security questions, offers excuses or substitutes, or pushes urgency exactly when asked to verify ('I don't have that on me, can we just do it quickly').
triggers: forgot the answer to my security
dont have that in front of me
dont have it in front of me
can we just do it quickly
can we just do this quickly
do we have to do this
do we really need to do this
i dont have time for this
i dont have time for questions
why do you need to know
patterns.suggested_agent_action: Do not bypass or shortcut verification, however urgent the caller sounds. Offer an alternative channel: a callback to the number already on file or an in-branch visit with ID.
patterns.say_this: I'm not able to skip verification, but I can call you back on the number on file or help you at a branch with ID.
